reviewer: Claude Code (AI assistant). Not an independent human review.
method: A sweep of every page of the year for passages shared word for word by 4 or more papers that no counted opening of round one explains; each passage read, looked up in the year's lists and counted by its own opening words against every page in both transcriptions, by the thin-year rule (Y-THIN as amended on 23 November 2026: items printed by every newspaper that survives for their weeks are admitted; single paragraphs from runs of news counted by their own words, C-09); the items printed by every surviving paper admitted at the owner's word of 25 November 2026; scan checks of each admitted passage
scan_scope: Each crop covers the excerpt, the opening of the printed item. Long documents were not proofread in full.

new_groups.label: London, June 1799: 'The treasures plundered from Rome, Naples, and Tuscany, by the French, are stated to have fallen into the hands of the Austrians'
new_groups.definition: Printings of a sentence of the London news of June 1799: 'The treasures plundered from Rome, Naples, and Tuscany, by the French, are stated to have fallen into the hands of the Austrians at Parma.' A paragraph of the London news, as the papers reprinted it; the Portland Gazette and the New Hampshire Gazette end it at 'the Austrians', and the Providence Journal prints 'at Parmo'.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1799 printings, checked against the scan (round two: printed by every paper that survives for its weeks, found by the sweep check of 24-25 November 2026 and admitted at the owner's word).

new_groups.label: Milan, 12 June 1799: 'After Moreau had detached Generals Victor and Grenier to Genoa ... They then dislodged General Ott, near Pontremoli'
new_groups.definition: Printings of a dated paragraph of the Milan news of June 1799, under 'June 12.': 'After Moreau had detached Generals Victor and Grenier to Genoa, Gen. V. marched to the valley of Taro, to co-operate with Macdonald. They then dislodged General Ott, near Pontremoli, and beat him back as far as Parma.' A paragraph of the news from Italy, as the London papers gave it and the papers reprinted it, after the paragraph on General Bellegarde; the Gazette of the United States prints 'valley of Tora' and 'General Otto', and the Portland Gazette 'Grenter'.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1799 printings, checked against the scan (round two: printed by every paper that survives for its weeks, found by the sweep check of 24-25 November 2026 and admitted at the owner's word).

new_groups.label: Verona, 14 June 1799: 'In order to cover Macdonald's march by Sarzana to Genoa' ... 'Suwarrow is hastening with the main army towards Genoa'
new_groups.definition: Printings of a paragraph of the news from Italy dated Verona, 14 June 1799: 'In order to cover Macdonald's march by Sarzana to Genoa, Gen. Montrichard was obliged to make a movement with 8000 men against Modena; but Gen. Hohenzollern has repulsed him. General Otto is now collecting his whole force to encounter the enemy; and General Suwarow is hastening with the main army towards Genoa, to support him.' A paragraph of the news from Italy, as the London papers gave it and the papers reprinted it; the New Hampshire Gazette and the Providence Journal print 'has repulsed General Ott, who is now collecting', and the Portland Gazette prints the paragraph abridged (C-02).
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1799 printings, checked against the scan (round two: printed by every paper that survives for its weeks, found by the sweep check of 24-25 November 2026 and admitted at the owner's word).

dispositions_summary.method: Round two of 1799. The sweep check of 24 and 25 November 2026 (X-THIN-SWEEP; outputs/story_discovery_1779/sweep_check_25nov.md) read every passage of the 1799 pages shared word for word by 4 or more papers that no counted opening of round one explains, looked each up in the year's lists and counted it by its own opening words against every page of the year in both transcriptions. It found four items printed by every paper that survives for their weeks (the weeks of July to October, when four papers survive, X-1799-01), which round one's lists did not name; asked, the owner chose on 25 November 2026 to admit them as the rule reads. Every printing was checked against its page scan by AI reviewers (scan_batches/round2.json, SCAN_PROTOCOL.md; verdicts in scan_verdicts/round2*.json).
dispositions_summary.selection_rule: As in round one (Y-THIN as amended, B1, and X-1799-01): an item printed by every newspaper that survives for its weeks is admitted; single paragraphs from runs of news are counted by their own words (C-09). Each of the four is printed by all 4 papers of its weeks.

counted_item_by_item.Verona, 14 June: 4 of 4 on the same pages, counted by its own opening; the New Hampshire Gazette and the Providence Journal print 'has repulsed General Ott, who is now collecting' where the Gazette of the United States has 'has repulsed him. General Otto is now collecting', and the Portland Gazette prints the paragraph abridged (C-02).
counted_item_by_item.Mr. Adams: 4 of 4 (PG 30 September, NHG 1 October, GUS 2 October, PJ 9 October), counted by its own words; in the Portland Gazette the sentence closes a Boston summary of the London news to 12 August (a digest, C-09) and is counted as a printing of the sentence; in the other three it is a paragraph of its own.
